correctness.rationale: For complex c00, hereditary F allows A_theta={alpha in F:Re(e^{-i theta}x_alpha)>=0}; this belongs to F and Re(e^{-i theta}sum_{A_theta} x_alpha) is the sum of positive parts. Integrate theta: (2pi)^-1 int max(Re(e^{-i theta}z),0)dtheta=|z|/pi. Supremum over F gives ||Tx||infty >=||x||_F/pi; triangle yields norm <=1 and any singleton gives norm exactly 1. Extension to completed X_F is well-defined, continuous into C(closure F) and injective by density and lower bound. F_m=P([m]) plus remote singletons is hereditary and covers N; unit roots of unity on first m have F-norm m. For every subset, project onto the sum direction and bound by the vector sum of a consecutive block of mth roots, at most csc(pi/m). Thus inverse ratio >=m sin(pi/m)->pi, giving true sharp universal constant. Independently enumerated all 2^m subsets for m=3,5,7,9,12; each max fell under csc(pi/m) and ratios approached pi. Finite checks are not the proof.
residual_risks: The sharpness is asymptotic across families; no individual X_F is asserted to realize pi.
One must define Tx on the completion by continuous extension, not by unjustified absolute summation over arbitrary infinite A.

value.rationale: A canonical embedding from any complex combinatorial Banach space into a compact C(K) space is structurally important in the original paper. The exact universal complex inverse bound pi, nontrivial sharpness for a single natural map, and explicit extremal hereditary families quantify representation geometry across arbitrary cardinals; the contrast with the source real constant 2 is a natural full scalar-field counterpart. Value is in the precise canonical distortion theorem, not a generic observation that a subset sum is large.
residual_risks: The particular numerical constant follows from a classical planar half-plane average, but transferring it sharply to every hereditary F and C(closure F) has a well-defined independent use.
